# Vibe Aegis - Complete Framework (Single-Fetch Document)

> This is the self-contained edition of the Vibe Aegis repository. Everything an AI agent
> needs to understand and execute the framework is below: the full README, the always-on
> engineering rules, all three skill definitions, the scanner CLI reference, and the JSON
> report schema. Reading this one document is equivalent to reading the whole repository.
>
> Canonical repository: https://github.com/Tacuns/vibe-aegis
> Structured index: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Tacuns/vibe-aegis/main/llms.txt
> License: MIT
> Scope: Defensive pre-deployment auditing of applications you own. Live `--url` checks are
> passive, read-only HTTP GET requests.

## How An Agent Should Use This Document

1. Read the **6-Stage Adversarial Analysis Loop** to learn the protocol.
2. Run the deterministic scanner (`scripts/aegis_scan.py`) first - it is free of LLM cost and
   fingerprints the stack for you.
3. Execute Stage 2 using the `security-redteam-loop` skill and Stage 3 using the
   `ui-ux-bug-finder` skill, both reproduced in full below.
4. Apply the Skeptic stage to disprove your own findings before reporting any of them.
5. Write `.aegis/AUDIT_REPORT.md` with the Release Readiness Score.
6. Never modify source files without the user's explicit approval.

# 🛡️ Vibe Aegis (`vibe-aegis`)

**The 10-Stage First-to-Last Full-Stack Safeguard for Vibe-Coded Apps — across 8 domains.**

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Python 3.8+ Zero-Deps](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-3.8%2B%20zero--deps-3776AB?logo=python&logoColor=white)](scripts/aegis_scan.py)
[![Node >= 18 NPX CLI](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node-%3E%3D18%20npx%20CLI-339933?logo=node.js&logoColor=white)](bin/vibe-aegis.mjs)
[![CI](https://github.com/Tacuns/vibe-aegis/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/Tacuns/vibe-aegis/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

## ⚡ Start in 2 Lines (Paste into Any AI Agent)

Open your project in **Claude Code, VS Code Copilot, OpenAI Codex, Cursor, Windsurf, Cline, Gemini CLI**, ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity or Grok — and paste this. Nothing to clone, nothing to install first:

```text
Read https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Tacuns/vibe-aegis/main/llms.txt and run the Vibe Aegis setup and 10-stage Security + UI/UX audit in this project.
```

That single URL teaches the agent the whole framework. For everything in one fetch, point it at [`llms-full.txt`](llms-full.txt) instead.

**Prefer a plugin?**

```text
/plugin marketplace add Tacuns/vibe-aegis        # Claude Code, then type /aegis
codex plugin marketplace add Tacuns/vibe-aegis   # OpenAI Codex, then type $vibe-aegis
```

---

AI coding assistants build features at lightning speed, but they routinely ship hidden security holes (exposed client secrets, missing Row-Level Security, IDOR, unverified webhooks, prompt injection) and broken UI/UX states (dead placeholder buttons, missing loading/disabled states, mobile overflow traps, WCAG accessibility failures).

**Vibe Aegis** combines a **zero-dependency static + live deployment scanner** (`aegis_scan.py`) with a **10-stage adversarial multi-agent analysis loop across 8 domains** that installs in one command across **Claude Code, VS Code (GitHub Copilot), OpenAI Codex, Cursor, Windsurf, Cline, Gemini CLI, and OpenCode**.


## 🧭 The 8 Domains

A single pass over eight separate failure modes. Each has its own skill, its own rules, and its own place in the 10-stage loop.

| # | Domain | Catches | Skill |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | **Architecture & Tenancy** | Broken tenant isolation, missing RLS, weak trust boundaries | `architecture-threat-model` |
| 2 | **Application Security** | Secrets, IDOR, injection, XSS, SSRF, auth & session flaws | `security-redteam-loop` |
| 3 | **Payments & Business Logic** | Client-trusted prices, replayable webhooks, double-spend races | `payments-logic-auditor` |
| 4 | **AI / LLM** | Prompt injection, denial-of-wallet, unsafe output, tool scope | `ai-llm-security-shield` |
| 5 | **Backend Reliability** | Unbounded queries, N+1 loops, missing timeouts, PII in logs | `backend-reliability-scale` |
| 6 | **UI/UX & Accessibility** | Dead buttons, missing async states, mobile overflow, WCAG 2.2 AA | `ui-ux-bug-finder` |
| 7 | **Shipped Artifacts** | Secrets in the built bundle, source maps, unsigned/debuggable APKs | `artifact-leak-hunter` |
| 8 | **Production Readiness** | Headers, exposed files, container & CI hardening, go/no-go verdict | `production-preflight-gate` |

Security bugs leak data. **Payment bugs leak money.** **Reliability bugs only appear the day you succeed.** They need separate passes, because each one looks fine from inside the others.

## 🔄 The Adversarial Analysis Loop

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["🔍 Stage 1 — Recon & Triage<br/>aegis_scan.py<br/>Fingerprint stack · 40+ deterministic rules"]
    B["🛡️ Stage 2 — Security Hunter<br/>Secrets · Auth & IDOR · RLS<br/>Payments · SSRF · AI/LLM"]
    C["🎨 Stage 3 — UI/UX Hunter<br/>Dead controls · Async states<br/>Mobile overflow · WCAG 2.2 AA"]
    D["🤔 Stage 4 — Adversarial Skeptic<br/>Try to DISPROVE every claim<br/>middleware · ORM · auto-escaping"]
    E["⚖️ Stage 5 — Evidence Referee<br/>CONFIRMED · MANUAL_REVIEW · DISMISSED<br/>CWE · CVSS · Readiness Score 0-100"]
    F{"Score >= 90 and zero<br/>CRITICAL / HIGH?"}
    G["✅ READY TO PUBLISH"]
    H["🔧 Stage 6 — Guarded Fixer --fix<br/>Branch · patch one at a time<br/>re-scan + rebuild · auto-revert regressions"]

    A --> B
    A --> C
    B --> D
    C --> D
    D --> E
    E --> F
    F -->|Yes| G
    F -->|No| H
    H --> A

    style A fill:#1e3a8a,stroke:#3b82f6,color:#fff
    style B fill:#7f1d1d,stroke:#ef4444,color:#fff
    style C fill:#713f12,stroke:#f59e0b,color:#fff
    style D fill:#4c1d95,stroke:#8b5cf6,color:#fff
    style E fill:#164e63,stroke:#06b6d4,color:#fff
    style F fill:#374151,stroke:#9ca3af,color:#fff
    style G fill:#14532d,stroke:#22c55e,color:#fff
    style H fill:#78350f,stroke:#f97316,color:#fff
```

1. **Stage 1 — Deterministic Recon & Triage (`scripts/aegis_scan.py`)**
   Runs the fast local scanner to fingerprint your stack (frameworks, auth, database, payment provider, UI library), map trust boundaries, and produce `.aegis/scan-report.json` with zero LLM token waste.
2. **Stage 2 — Deep Security Hunter (`skills/security-redteam-loop/SKILL.md`)**
   Traces every entry point, API route, Server Action, database query, webhook, and environment variable from **Low to Critical** severity using STRIDE threat modeling and OWASP Top 10 + AI-specific vulnerability rules.
3. **Stage 3 — Deep UI/UX Design & Flow Bug Finder (`skills/ui-ux-bug-finder/SKILL.md`)**
   Audits every page and component for dead click handlers (`href="#"`, empty `onClick`), missing async `loading`/`disabled` states (double-submit bugs), missing empty/error states, responsive overflow traps, z-index collisions, and WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility violations. If `agent-browser` or Playwright is available, it also inspects the live rendered DOM across mobile (`375x812`) and desktop (`1440x900`) viewports.
4. **Stage 4 — Adversarial Skeptic (False-Positive Filter)**
   Challenges every claim from Stages 2 and 3 by checking middleware (`middleware.ts`), ORM parameterization, framework auto-escaping, and parent layout containers. Any speculative claim without a reachable trigger is dismissed.
5. **Stage 5 — Evidence Referee & Release Readiness Scorecard**
   Assigns final verdicts (`CONFIRMED`, `MANUAL_REVIEW`, `DISMISSED`), CWE IDs, CVSS 3.1 / UX severity scores, and calculates a **0–100 Release Readiness Score** inside `.aegis/AUDIT_REPORT.md`. Publishing is blocked if any `CRITICAL` or `HIGH` issue remains open.
6. **Stage 6 — Guarded Fixer & Verification Loop (Opt-In `--fix`)**
   Creates a safe git branch (`aegis/hardening-<timestamp>`), patches confirmed bugs one by one, re-runs `aegis_scan.py` plus your project's build/test suite after each patch, and automatically reverts any fix that introduces a regression.

## ⚡ Why Vibe Aegis?

| Capability | Single-Skill Security Checklists | Binary Reverse-Engineering Tools | **Vibe Aegis (`vibe-aegis`)** |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Pre-Publish Vibe-Code Security Gate** | Partial (15–30 static rules) | No (focused on binary/app decompilation) | **40+ Static + Live HTTP Posture Checks (Low to Critical)** |
| **Adversarial Verification Loop** | Single-pass prompt (high false positives) | Evidence tracing only | **10 stages: Hunter → Skeptic → Referee → Guarded Fixer** |
| **UI/UX Design & Browser QA Bug Finder** | None | None | **Detects dead buttons, missing async loading states, mobile overflow, a11y & visual bugs** |
| **Stack-Aware Rules** | Basic | JS/Electron/Native | **Next.js, React, Supabase, Firebase, Prisma, Stripe, Razorpay, FastAPI, Express, Mobile** |
| **Universal Agent Support** | 1–2 agents | MCP clients | **Claude Code, VS Code, Codex, Cursor, Windsurf, Cline, Gemini CLI, GitHub Actions** |
| **Machine-Readable Output** | Prose only | Tool-specific | **`.aegis/scan-report.json` validated by a published JSON Schema** |

## 🚀 Install Options

### Option 1: Universal Shell Installer (macOS / Linux / WSL / Git Bash)

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Tacuns/vibe-aegis.git
cd vibe-aegis

# Install into a project for ALL agents (Claude Code, VS Code Copilot, Codex, Cursor, Windsurf, Cline, Gemini)
bash install.sh --target /path/to/your/app --agent all

# Or install globally for your user profile
bash install.sh --global --agent all
```

### Option 2: `npx` CLI Installer (Node.js 18+)

```bash
npx vibe-aegis setup --target . --agent all

# Or select a specific agent: claude-code | vscode | codex | cursor | windsurf | cline | gemini
npx vibe-aegis setup --target . --agent claude-code
```

### Option 3: Run the Deterministic Scanner Directly (Python 3.8+, Zero Dependencies)

```bash
# 1. Full static codebase audit (Security + UI/UX bugs)
python3 scripts/aegis_scan.py /path/to/your/app

# 2. Scan codebase + verify live/staging URL headers, CORS & exposed files (.env, .git)
python3 scripts/aegis_scan.py /path/to/your/app --url https://staging.yourapp.com

# 3. Export structured JSON report for CI/CD or agent ingestion
python3 scripts/aegis_scan.py /path/to/your/app --json --output .aegis/scan-report.json

# 4. CI gate — exit code 1 if any CRITICAL or HIGH finding exists
python3 scripts/aegis_scan.py /path/to/your/app --fail-on-high
```

### Scanner CLI Reference

**Output**

| Argument | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `target` | Path to the repository to scan (default `.`) |
| `--json` | Print the full JSON report to stdout |
| `--output <PATH>` | Write the JSON report to a file (parent directories are created) |
| `--sarif <PATH>` | Write SARIF 2.1.0 so findings appear in GitHub's Security tab |
| `--sbom <PATH>` | Write a CycloneDX 1.5 SBOM of all detected dependencies |
| `--quiet` | Print only the one-line summary |

**Release gate**

| Argument | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `--fail-on-high` | Exit `1` if any `CRITICAL` or `HIGH` finding exists |
| `--fail-on <level>` | Exit `1` at or above `critical`/`high`/`medium`/`low` |
| `--include-tests` | Also audit test and fixture files (excluded by default — they contain deliberately insecure code) |
| `--fail-on-incomplete` | Exit `1` if any check could not run — use when a green pipeline must mean *fully audited*, not merely *nothing found* |

**Scope — how you adopt this on a real codebase**

| Argument | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `--diff [REF]` | Scan only files changed vs `REF` (default `origin/main`). Ideal for pull requests |
| `--baseline <PATH>` | Suppress findings recorded in a baseline file |
| `--write-baseline <PATH>` | Accept every current finding as pre-existing, so future scans show only new issues |

**Deep analysis**

| Argument | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `--artifact [PATH]` | Verify a build directory or an `.apk`/`.aab`/`.ipa`. Auto-detects `dist/`, `build/`, `.next/` |
| `--git-history [N]` | Hunt credentials committed in the last `N` commits (default 300) |
| `--deps` | Check dependencies against the OSV vulnerability database |
| `--url <URL>` | Passive, read-only live header & exposure checks |
| `--all` | Enable artifacts + git history + dependencies |
| `--offline` | Never make a network request |

**What leaves your machine.** The scanner is offline by default and sends nothing anywhere —
there is no telemetry, ever. Exactly two flags make a network request, and both are opt-in:

| Flag | Request | What is disclosed |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `--deps` (also via `--all`) | `POST https://api.osv.dev/v1/querybatch` | Your dependency **names and versions** — not your source, not your file names |
| `--url <URL>` | `GET` against the URL you supply | Nothing of yours; it reads your own deployment's headers |

`--offline` hard-disables both. A stage that could not reach the network is recorded as a
coverage gap (`DEP-00` / `LIVE-00`) and **blocks** a `READY TO PUBLISH` verdict rather than
silently passing.

**Credentials in reports are redacted** to first 6 + last 4 characters before anything is
written, so `.aegis/scan-report.json` is safe to commit, attach to an issue, or upload as a
CI artifact.

**Exit codes:** `0` success · `1` blocking findings with a gate flag · `2` target path does not exist.

Also honoured: a `.aegis-ignore` file in the repo root, one entry per line — either a rule id (`SEC-03`) or a path glob (`src/legacy/**`).

## 🔍 Complete Audit Coverage Matrix (Low to Critical)

### A. Security & Architecture Safeguards

| ID | Category | Severity | What Vibe Aegis Catches |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `SEC-01` | **Client-Exposed Secrets** | Critical | Private keys or tokens in `NEXT_PUBLIC_`, `VITE_`, `EXPO_PUBLIC_`, `REACT_APP_`, or hardcoded in source files |
| `SEC-02` | **Database RLS Disabled** | Critical | Supabase/PostgreSQL tables without `ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` or permissive `USING (true)` policies; Firebase `allow read, write: if true` |
| `SEC-03` | **Unprotected API / Server Actions** | Critical | Next.js `/api/*` routes, `"use server"` actions, FastAPI, or Express mutations lacking session/auth verification |
| `SEC-04` | **Broken Access Control (IDOR)** | Critical | Queries fetching/mutating records by user-supplied `id` without scoping to `auth.uid()` / authenticated session owner |
| `SEC-05` | **Payment & Checkout Tampering** | Critical | Trusting client-submitted prices, plan tiers, or quantities in Stripe/Razorpay checkout sessions |
| `SEC-06` | **Unverified Webhooks** | Critical | Payment or auth webhooks processing payloads without cryptographic signature verification (`stripe.webhooks.constructEvent`) |
| `SEC-07` | **SQL / Raw Query Injection** | High | String interpolation in SQL, `prisma.$queryRawUnsafe()`, `sequelize.query()`, or Python `cursor.execute(f"...")` |
| `SEC-08` | **Command & Code Injection** | High | Unsanitized input passed to `child_process.exec`, `eval()`, `new Function()`, `os.system()`, or `subprocess(..., shell=True)` |
| `SEC-09` | **Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)** | High | Unsanitized `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, `v-html`, `innerHTML`, or `javascript:` URLs in user-controlled hrefs |
| `SEC-10` | **JWT & Session Flaws** | High | `jwt.decode()` used without `jwt.verify()`, weak JWT secrets, or sensitive auth tokens stored in `localStorage` |
| `SEC-11` | **Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)** | High | Server endpoints fetching user-supplied URLs without allowlisting or private-IP (`127.0.0.1`, `169.254.169.254`) blocking |
| `SEC-12` | **AI / LLM Prompt Injection & Spend** | High | Unbounded LLM endpoints without auth, rate limiting, max-token caps, or system/user prompt boundary separation |
| `SEC-13` | **Wildcard CORS & CSRF** | High | `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` combined with credentials, or cookie-authenticated state changes lacking CSRF protection |
| `SEC-14` | **Missing Rate Limiting** | Medium | Auth login, OTP, password reset, AI generation, and email endpoints lacking IP/user rate limiters |
| `SEC-15` | **Insecure File Uploads** | Medium | Upload handlers accepting arbitrary MIME types, missing size limits, or storing files with user-supplied paths (path traversal) |
| `SEC-16` | **Supply-Chain & Slopsquatting** | Medium | Unpinned dependencies, suspicious AI-hallucinated package names, or lockfile mismatches |
| `SEC-17` | **Live Posture & Exposed Artifacts** | Low–Crit | Publicly reachable `.env`, `.git/config`, `.map` source maps, debug endpoints, or missing CSP / HSTS / `X-Frame-Options` headers |

### B. UI/UX Design & Frontend QA Bug Finder

**The element must match the behaviour.** If it performs an action it is a `<button>`; if it navigates it is an `<a>` with a real `href`. Get that right and the browser supplies focus, Tab order, Enter *and* Space, and the correct screen-reader role for free — no `role`, `tabIndex` or `onKeyDown` needed. These three rules are separated because each has a different fix.

| ID | Category | Severity | What Vibe Aegis Catches |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `UX-01` | **Dead Buttons & Placeholder Links** | High | A control that does nothing: `<a href="#">` with no handler, or `onClick={() => {}}` / `console.log` stubs |
| `UX-11` | **Action Rendered As A Link** | High | `<a href="#" onClick={...}>` or `href="javascript:"` — works with a mouse, but screen readers announce "link", Space does not activate it, and the page jumps to top. Use `<button>` |
| `UX-12` | **Clickable `div` / `span`** | High | An `onClick` on a non-interactive element with no `role` or `tabIndex` — unreachable by Tab, unusable by keyboard, announced as plain text |
| `UX-02` | **Missing Async Loading / Disabled State** | High | Async form submissions or mutation buttons that don't disable during flight, allowing duplicate charges or duplicate records |
| `UX-03` | **Silent Catch & Missing Error Feedback** | High | `catch (err) {}` blocks that swallow API failures without showing a toast, inline error message, or fallback UI |
| `UX-04` | **Missing Empty & Skeleton States** | Medium | `.map()` list renders that show a blank screen when the array is empty (`length === 0`) or loading |
| `UX-05` | **Mobile Viewport & Overflow Traps** | Medium | Fixed pixel widths (`w-[600px]`, `min-w-[500px]`, `width: 700px`) and `100vw` containers causing horizontal scrollbars on mobile |
| `UX-06` | **Form Accessibility & Validation Gaps** | Medium | `<input>`, `<select>`, or `<textarea>` missing associated `<label>`, `id`/`name`, or accessible error states |
| `UX-07` | **Icon Buttons & Image Accessibility** | Medium | Icon-only buttons without `aria-label` and `<img>` tags missing `alt` attributes |
| `UX-08` | **Focus Ring Suppression** | Low | `outline-none` or `outline: 0` applied without a replacement `focus-visible:ring` keyboard indicator |
| `UX-09` | **Unfinished AI Placeholders in UI** | High | Leftover `"Lorem ipsum"`, `"TODO:"`, `"placeholder"`, `"example.com"`, or fake `$99,999` mock metrics in production views |
| `UX-10` | **Z-Index & Modal Scroll Traps** | Low | Arbitrary `z-[99999]` collisions or modals that lock `document.body.style.overflow` without cleanup on unmount |

### C. Payments & Business Logic

| ID | Category | Severity | What it catches |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `PAY-01` | Client-trusted price | Critical | `amount`, `unit_amount`, `price`, `quantity`, `currency` or `discount` taken from the request body |
| `PAY-02` | Non-atomic balance update | High | Read-then-write on credits or balances — two parallel requests both succeed (double-spend) |
| `PAY-03` | Unverified webhook | Critical | Payment webhook without signature verification against the raw body |

### D. Backend Reliability & Privacy

| ID | Category | Severity | What it catches |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `REL-01` | Unbounded query | Medium | `findMany()` with no `take` — fine at 100 rows, fatal at 100,000 |
| `REL-02` | N+1 query loop | Medium | A database `await` inside a `for` loop or `.map(async …)` |
| `REL-03` | Sensitive data in logs | High | Passwords, tokens, API keys or PII passed to `console.log` or a logger |
| `REL-04` | Missing timeout | Medium | `await fetch()` with no `AbortSignal.timeout()` — a hung upstream eats your concurrency |

`REL` findings are reported at `MEDIUM` confidence: a pattern cannot know your data volume, so the Skeptic stage confirms against real table sizes.

### E. Data-Flow Analysis (follows the value, not the pattern)

A regex says *"there is a template literal in a query."* Taint analysis says *"**this** value came from the request and reaches **that** query unvalidated."* Input is traced from request sources (`req.body`, `req.json()`, `searchParams.get`, `formData.get`, route `params`) through assignments to dangerous sinks. A value that passes a validator (`zod.parse`, `parseInt`, `encodeURIComponent`, an allowlist check) is treated as clean and **not** reported.

| ID | Flow | Severity |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `FLOW-01` | Request input reaches a raw SQL query | Critical |
| `FLOW-02` | Request input reaches a shell or code-execution sink | Critical |
| `FLOW-03` | Request input reaches an HTML rendering sink | High |
| `FLOW-04` | Request input reaches a server-side fetch (SSRF) | High |
| `FLOW-05` | Request input reaches a filesystem path | High |

Reported at `MEDIUM` confidence by design — the tracker works within a function scope, so the Skeptic stage confirms before anything is called CONFIRMED.

### F. Shipped-Artifact Verification (what your users actually receive)

Source code says what you wrote. The build output says what ships. Because the scanner already read your source, it can **cross-reference** — turning a guess into proof.

| ID | Category | Severity | What it proves |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ART-01` | **Confirmed secret leak** | Critical | A credential from your source is present in the shipped bundle. Confirmed by construction |
| `ART-02` | Source map shipped | Medium / Low | With `sourcesContent`, your original unminified source reaches every visitor |
| `ART-03` | Credential in bundle | Critical–Medium | A provider-format key found directly in shipped JS/HTML/JSON |
| `ART-11` | Unsigned package | High | No signature block under `META-INF/` |
| `ART-12` | Config bundled in app | Critical | `.env`, `id_rsa` or `service-account.json` inside the `.apk`/`.aab`/`.ipa` |
| `ART-13` | Cleartext traffic | Medium | Manifest references cleartext HTTP |
| `ART-14` | Debuggable release | Medium | The `debuggable` attribute appears in the manifest. A binary manifest stores the *value* separately, so correct `debuggable="false"` hardening looks identical — verify with `aapt dump badging` |
| `ART-15` | Credential in package | Critical–Medium | A key embedded in packaged assets, resources or code |

### G. Supply Chain & Git History

| ID | Category | Severity | What it catches |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `DEP-01` | Known dependency vulnerability | Medium | Package versions with OSV advisories (npm, PyPI, crates.io, Go) |
| `HIST-01` | Credential in git history | Critical–Medium | A key committed at any point — **even if deleted later**, it is still readable and still compromised |

### Rule Variants

Some rules have narrower sub-variants, reported with their own id so you can suppress them individually:

| ID | Covers |
| :--- | :--- |
| `SEC-01B` | Secret-named value exposed through a client-bundled env prefix |
| `SEC-01C` | `.env` present in the project root but not in `.gitignore` |
| `SEC-02B` | Permissive Firebase / Firestore rule (`allow read, write: if true`) |
| `SEC-10B` | Auth token stored in `localStorage` rather than an HttpOnly cookie |
| `SEC-17B` | `/.env` or `/.git/config` publicly reachable on the live server |
| `DEP-00`, `LIVE-00`, `GIT-00`, `ART-10` | **Coverage gaps**, not defects — a check that could not run. Any id ending `-00` is always a gap |

### Secret Detection Precision

A noisy scanner gets uninstalled. Credential rules only fire on real provider key shapes (AWS, Stripe, GitHub, Google, Slack, OpenAI, Anthropic, SendGrid, Twilio, Razorpay, npm, PEM private keys, Supabase service-role JWTs, database URLs with inline credentials) or on secret-named variables holding high-entropy values. Placeholders such as `your-api-key-here`, `changeme`, `${process.env.X}` and AWS's own documentation key `AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE` are rejected.

**Every credential in every report is redacted** to its first 6 and last 4 characters, so `.aegis/scan-report.json` is safe to commit, attach to an issue, or hand to an agent.

### Fail-Closed: Coverage Is Not Severity

A check that **could not run** is an unknown, not a pass. The gate fails closed:

| Condition | Verdict |
| :--- | :--- |
| 0 source files scanned | `INCOMPLETE_SCAN` — score forced to 0 |
| Any `CRITICAL` / `HIGH` open | `BLOCKED` |
| Any check skipped or errored | `VERIFIED_PARTIAL - INCOMPLETE_SCAN` |
| Score < 90, nothing skipped | `NEEDS REVIEW` |
| Files scanned · nothing skipped · no `CRITICAL`/`HIGH` · score ≥ 90 | **`READY TO PUBLISH`** |

`READY TO PUBLISH` requires **all four** conditions. Pass `allow_skipped=True` to `compute_readiness_score()` to override deliberately.

Called in isolation, `compute_readiness_score([DEP-00])` also fails closed — any rule id ending `-00` is treated as a coverage gap regardless of how the `Finding` was built. Skipped checks (offline mode, an unreachable URL or OSV, an unopenable package) are reported separately in `skipped_checks`, never counted in the score, and they force the verdict to `INCOMPLETE`:

```text
Readiness Score  : 100/100 - INCOMPLETE (1 check did not run: Dependency
                   Vulnerability Check Skipped). Not certified.

CHECKS THAT DID NOT RUN (1) - result UNKNOWN, not clean:
  - Dependency Vulnerability Check Skipped (offline mode)
```

`READY TO PUBLISH` is only ever issued for a **complete** audit. Use `--fail-on-incomplete` to enforce that in CI.

### Release Readiness Score

The scanner starts at **100** and subtracts **25** per `CRITICAL`, **10** per `HIGH`, **4** per `MEDIUM` and **1** per `LOW`, floored at `0`.

| Condition | Verdict |
| :--- | :--- |
| Any open `CRITICAL` or `HIGH` | `BLOCKED (Fix Critical/High findings before publishing)` |
| Score ≥ 90, no blockers | `READY TO PUBLISH` |
| Score < 90, no blockers | `NEEDS REVIEW (Address Medium/Low polish items)` |

See [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md) for the rule-authoring guide and severity rubric.

## ⚖️ Responsible Use & Scope

Vibe Aegis is a **defensive pre-deployment security and UI/UX quality assurance framework**. Its live URL posture checks (`--url`) perform strictly passive, read-only HTTP `GET` requests to inspect security headers and accidental file exposure. It sends no payloads and no credentials.

**Only scan applications and deployments that you own or have explicit authorization to test.** See [`SECURITY.md`](SECURITY.md) for the full scope statement and vulnerability reporting process.

# =============================================================================
# PART 2: AGENTS.md - ALWAYS-ON ENGINEERING RULES
# =============================================================================

These rules apply while code is being written, not only during an audit. The installer
places this file as `AGENTS.md`, `.cursorrules`, `.clinerules`, `GEMINI.md` and
`.windsurf/rules/vibe-aegis.md`.

# 🛡️ Vibe Aegis — Always-On Security & UI/UX Engineering Rules

You are operating in a repository protected by **Vibe Aegis**. Every code change you write or review must satisfy both **Defensive Security Rules** and **UI/UX Production Quality Rules** before completion.

## 1. Non-Negotiable Security Rules (Prevent Vulnerabilities While Writing Code)

1. **Zero Client-Side Secrets (`SEC-01`)**:
   - Never place private API keys, database URLs, service-role keys, or webhook secrets in client-exposed variables (`NEXT_PUBLIC_*`, `VITE_*`, `EXPO_PUBLIC_*`, `REACT_APP_*`) or source files.
   - Keep `.env`, `.env.local`, and `.env.*` in `.gitignore`. Only commit `.env.example` with blank placeholders.
2. **Database Row-Level Security & Ownership Scoping (`SEC-02`, `SEC-04`)**:
   - Every Supabase/PostgreSQL table storing user or tenant data must run `ALTER TABLE <name> ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;` with explicit `SELECT`, `INSERT`, `UPDATE`, and `DELETE` policies scoped to `auth.uid()`. Never use `USING (true)` on non-public tables.
   - Every database read, update, or delete by ID must filter by the authenticated user's session ID or tenant ID (preventing IDOR).
3. **Server-Side Authentication & Input Validation (`SEC-03`, `SEC-07`, `SEC-08`)**:
   - Authenticate every API route, Server Action (`"use server"`), and RPC handler on the server. UI route hiding or client-side checks are never a security boundary.
   - Validate all external inputs (body, query, params, headers) using schema validators (e.g., `zod`, `pydantic`) before touching business logic.
   - Always use parameterized queries or safe ORM methods. Never interpolate strings into SQL, `$queryRawUnsafe`, or shell commands (`exec`, `subprocess` with `shell=True`).
4. **Payments, Webhooks & Rate Limiting (`SEC-05`, `SEC-06`, `SEC-12`, `SEC-14`)**:
   - Never trust client-submitted prices, discounts, or plan IDs; look up pricing on the server from trusted product tables.
   - Verify cryptographic signatures on every incoming webhook (`stripe.webhooks.constructEvent`, HMAC verification) using the raw request body.
   - Enforce rate limiting and token/cost budgets on login, OTP, password reset, email, and AI/LLM generation endpoints.
5. **Safe Output Rendering & Headers (`SEC-09`, `SEC-10`, `SEC-13`)**:
   - Never render unsanitized HTML via `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, `v-html`, or `innerHTML`.
   - Store session tokens in `HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax/Strict` cookies—never in `localStorage`.

5. **Payments & Entitlements (`PAY-01`, `PAY-02`, `PAY-03`)**:
   - Never accept `amount`, `unit_amount`, `price`, `quantity`, `currency` or `discount` from the client. Take a plan or product ID and resolve the real price on the server.
   - Verify every webhook signature against the raw unparsed body, and store each processed `event.id` under a unique constraint so a replay cannot grant an entitlement twice.
   - Never read a balance, decide, then write it back. Use one atomic statement: `UPDATE wallets SET balance = balance - $1 WHERE user_id = $2 AND balance >= $1`, and treat zero affected rows as insufficient funds.
6. **Reliability & Privacy (`REL-01` to `REL-04`)**:
   - Every list query needs an explicit maximum page size. `findMany()` with no `take` loads the whole table into memory.
   - Never `await` a database call inside a loop. Batch with `WHERE id IN (...)` or a join.
   - Attach `AbortSignal.timeout(10000)` to outbound `fetch()` so a hung dependency cannot consume your concurrency budget.
   - Never log passwords, tokens, API keys or personal data. Log an identifier instead of the value.

## 2. Non-Negotiable UI/UX Quality Rules (Prevent Broken Frontend Experiences)

1. **Complete Interactive States (`UX-01`, `UX-02`, `UX-03`, `UX-04`)**:
   - Never leave dead buttons or placeholder links (`href="#"`, empty `onClick={() => {}}`, or `console.log` stubs). Every interactive control must wire to real behavior.
   - Every async button or form submission must disable during flight (`disabled={isLoading}`) and display a clear loading indicator to prevent double submissions.
   - Every data view or list must explicitly handle 4 states: **Loading** (skeleton/spinner), **Empty** (clear message + call-to-action), **Error** (actionable retry/error banner, never a silent `catch {}`), and **Populated**.
2. **Responsive Layout & Touch Ergonomics (`UX-05`, `UX-10`)**:
   - Design mobile-first (`320px–375px` up to `1440px+`). Never use rigid unguarded pixel widths (`w-[600px]`, `width: 800px`) that cause horizontal overflow on mobile screens.
   - Keep interactive touch targets at least `44x44px` on mobile and maintain a clear z-index scale for modals, dropdowns, and toasts.
3. **Accessibility Floor — WCAG 2.2 AA (`UX-06`, `UX-07`, `UX-08`)**:
   - Every form control (`<input>`, `<select>`, `<textarea>`) must have an associated `<label>` or `aria-label`.
   - Every icon-only button must include an `aria-label`, and every informative `<img>` must include a descriptive `alt` attribute.
   - Never remove keyboard focus rings (`outline-none`) without providing a high-contrast `focus-visible:ring` replacement.
4. **Zero Synthetic Placeholders in Production Views (`UX-09`)**:
   - Never ship `"Lorem ipsum"`, `"TODO"`, `"john@example.com"`, or hardcoded fake metrics in user-facing components.

## 3. Running the Vibe Aegis 10-Stage Pre-Publish Audit Loop

Before publishing or merging major features, run the full Vibe Aegis loop:

1. Execute `python3 .aegis/scripts/aegis_scan.py . --json --output .aegis/scan-report.json` (or `python3 scripts/aegis_scan.py .`).
2. Follow the orchestration workflow in `.claude/skills/vibe-aegis/SKILL.md` (or `.agents/skills/vibe-aegis/SKILL.md`):
   - **Recon** -> **Security Hunter** -> **UI/UX Hunter** -> **Adversarial Skeptic** -> **Evidence Referee** -> **Guarded Fixer**.
3. Write the final verified scorecard to `.aegis/AUDIT_REPORT.md`. Do not declare an app ready for production until all `CRITICAL` and `HIGH` confirmed findings are resolved.

# =============================================================================
# PART 3: SKILL - `vibe-aegis` (MASTER 6-STAGE ORCHESTRATOR)
# =============================================================================

Source file: `skills/vibe-aegis/SKILL.md`

---
name: vibe-aegis
description: Master 10-stage First-to-Last full-stack safeguard loop for vibe-coded apps across 8 domains. Orchestrates deterministic triage, deep Low-to-Critical security auditing, UI/UX design & browser bug finding, adversarial false-positive filtering (Skeptic), evidence grading (Referee), and guarded branch auto-fixing. Use whenever the user asks to audit, secure, test UI/UX, or prepare an app for production.
---

# Vibe Aegis — Master 10-Stage Pre-Launch Audit & Hardening Loop

Run a complete, adversarial pre-publication audit across both **Application Security (Low to Critical)** and **UI/UX Design & Functional Completeness** before any vibe-coded application ships to production.

## When to Trigger

- The user types `/aegis`, `/aegis-audit`, or `$vibe-aegis`
- The user asks to "check if my app is safe to publish", "find security holes and UI/UX bugs", "run a pre-launch audit", or "harden this vibe-coded app"

## The 8 Domains

| # | Domain | Skill |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | Architecture, tenancy & RLS | `architecture-threat-model` |
| 2 | Application security | `security-redteam-loop` |
| 3 | Payments & business logic | `payments-logic-auditor` |
| 4 | AI / LLM | `ai-llm-security-shield` |
| 5 | Backend reliability & scale | `backend-reliability-scale` |
| 6 | UI/UX & accessibility | `ui-ux-bug-finder` |
| 7 | Shipped artifacts | `artifact-leak-hunter` |
| 8 | Production readiness | `production-preflight-gate` |

## 10-Stage Execution Protocol

### Stage 1: Deterministic Recon & Triage (`aegis_scan.py`)

Run the bundled zero-dependency scanner first so you never waste context guessing the stack:

```bash
# Full sweep: source + data-flow + git history + dependencies + build artifacts
python3 .aegis/scripts/aegis_scan.py . --all --output .aegis/scan-report.json

# Fallback if running directly from the vibe-aegis repo:
python3 scripts/aegis_scan.py . --all --output .aegis/scan-report.json

# Reviewing a pull request? Scan only what changed, and suppress pre-existing noise:
python3 .aegis/scripts/aegis_scan.py . --diff origin/main --baseline .aegis/baseline.json
```

The scanner now reports six domains: `SECURITY`, `UI_UX`, `DATAFLOW` (request input traced
to a dangerous sink), `SUPPLY_CHAIN` (known dependency vulnerabilities), `ARTIFACT` (what the
build actually ships) and `HISTORY` (credentials committed at any point). Credentials in the
report are always redacted, so `.aegis/scan-report.json` is safe to attach to an issue.

Read `.aegis/scan-report.json` to extract:
1. Detected frameworks, database/BaaS, auth libraries, payment SDKs, UI libraries, and AI SDKs.
2. All deterministic `SECURITY` and `UI_UX` candidate findings.
3. Map all public entry points (`app/api/**`, `pages/api/**`, `"use server"` actions, webhooks, public routes, and database schema/migrations).

### Stage 1.5: Architecture, Tenancy & Threat Model

Load `skills/architecture-threat-model/SKILL.md`. Map entry points, trust boundaries, assets and
actors, verify tenant isolation and Row-Level Security, and write `.aegis/THREAT_MODEL.md`.

Do this **before** line-level hunting. Without the map, a missing `aria-label` and a missing tenant
filter look like two findings of similar size. They are not.

### Stage 2: Deep Security Red-Team Hunter (Low -> Critical)

Load and follow the instructions in `skills/security-redteam-loop/SKILL.md` (or `.claude/skills/security-redteam-loop/SKILL.md`).
- Trace data flows across files—do not stop at single-line regex matches.
- Verify authentication, ownership scoping (IDOR), Row-Level Security (RLS), payment price integrity, webhook signatures, SSRF, SQLi/XSS/CSRF, JWT verification, rate limits, and LLM token/cost caps.
- Record each candidate finding with exact `file:line`, concrete trigger path, STRIDE category, and CWE ID.

### Stage 2.5: Payments, Webhooks & Race Conditions

Load `skills/payments-logic-auditor/SKILL.md`. Security bugs leak data; payment bugs leak money
while the app appears to work. Check server-side pricing authority (`PAY-01`), webhook signature
verification and idempotency (`PAY-03`), and atomic balance updates (`PAY-02`).

### Stage 2.6: AI / LLM Security & Spend

Load `skills/ai-llm-security-shield/SKILL.md`. Confirm every model call has authentication, rate
limits, an input cap and an explicit `max_tokens`. Map every untrusted text source reaching a
prompt, follow model output to its sinks, and state the blast radius of a successful injection.

### Stage 2.7: Backend Reliability & Scale

Load `skills/backend-reliability-scale/SKILL.md`. Find the failures that only appear under real
traffic: unbounded queries, N+1 loops, missing indexes, serverless connection exhaustion, missing
timeouts, and personal data written to logs.

### Stage 3: Deep UI/UX Design & Browser QA Hunter

Load and follow the instructions in `skills/ui-ux-bug-finder/SKILL.md` (or `.claude/skills/ui-ux-bug-finder/SKILL.md`).
- Inspect every user-facing page, form, modal, and navigation component.
- Check for dead buttons (`href="#"`, empty `onClick`), missing async `disabled`/`loading` states (double-submit bugs), missing empty/error states, mobile viewport overflow (`320px–375px`), z-index collisions, and WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility issues.
- If a local dev server is running and `agent-browser` or Playwright is installed, open the live app and inspect both desktop (`1440x900`) and mobile (`375x812`) viewports plus the accessibility tree (`agent-browser snapshot`).

### Stage 3.5: Shipped-Artifact Verification

Load and follow `skills/artifact-leak-hunter/SKILL.md`. Source code says what you wrote; the
build output says what users receive. Cross-reference the credentials found in Stage 2 against
`dist/`, `.next/`, `build/` and any `.apk`/`.aab`/`.ipa`.

An `ART-01` finding is the one result in this framework that is **confirmed by construction** -
the same value is demonstrably present in both the source and the shipped bundle. Never downgrade
it, and always give the rotation-first remediation order.

### Stage 4: Adversarial Skeptic (False-Positive Elimination)

Switch perspective to the **Skeptic**. For every candidate finding from Stages 1–3:
- Attempt to **disprove** the claim by checking upstream middleware (`middleware.ts`), layout auth guards, ORM automatic parameterization, framework auto-escaping, or parent responsive containers.
- If a defence completely blocks the trigger, mark the finding `DISMISSED` and cite the exact defensive `file:line`.
- `DATAFLOW` findings are reported at `MEDIUM` confidence by design: the tracker works within a
  single function scope, so confirm the value really is attacker-controlled and really is unvalidated
  before promoting one to `CONFIRMED`.
- `ART-01` is the exception - it is already confirmed evidence and must not be dismissed.
- A publishable key (Supabase anon, Stripe publishable, Firebase web config) in a bundle is **not**
  a leak. Instead verify the protection it depends on: an anon key is only safe when Row-Level
  Security is enabled and enforced. Check that, and report on the RLS, not the key.

### Stage 5: Evidence Referee & Release Readiness Report

Switch perspective to the **Referee**. Evaluate all surviving claims and write `.aegis/AUDIT_REPORT.md` containing:
1. **Release Readiness Score (0–100)** and Release Gate Status (`READY TO PUBLISH` vs `BLOCKED`).
2. **Confirmed Security Findings Table** (ordered `CRITICAL` -> `HIGH` -> `MEDIUM` -> `LOW` with `file:line`, CWE, trigger explanation, and exact code fix).
3. **Confirmed UI/UX & Accessibility Findings Table** (ordered `HIGH` -> `MEDIUM` -> `LOW` with component location, visual/interaction impact, and exact code fix).
4. **Dismissed False Positives Log** (showing why each dismissed item is already safe).

### Stage 6: Guarded Auto-Fix & Verification Loop (When `--fix` or Remediation is Requested)

Never edit source files during a scan-only run without user approval. When the user requests `--fix` or approves remediation:
1. Create a dedicated git branch (`git checkout -b aegis/hardening-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M)`).
2. Apply minimal, surgical fixes for each `CONFIRMED` finding in priority order (`CRITICAL` -> `HIGH` -> `MEDIUM` -> `LOW`).
3. Re-run `python3 .aegis/scripts/aegis_scan.py .` and the project's native typecheck/test/build command (`npm run build`, `npm test`, or `pytest`).
4. If any patch introduces a build or test failure, immediately revert that commit and flag the item for `MANUAL_REVIEW`.
5. Repeat until the Release Readiness Score reaches `>= 90/100` with zero open `CRITICAL` or `HIGH` issues.

### Stage 7: Production Pre-Flight Gate

Load `skills/production-preflight-gate/SKILL.md`. The final go/no-go: live HTTP posture, exposed
artifacts, container and CI hardening, privacy and account-deletion readiness, and operational
readiness (rollback, monitoring, tested backups).

Issue exactly one verdict - `READY`, `READY WITH KNOWN LIMITATIONS` or `NOT READY` - and say for
each section what was checked, how, and what was **not** covered. Never issue `READY` because a
check was not run; mark it `NOT VERIFIED` and say so.

---

# =============================================================================
# PART 4: SKILL - `security-redteam-loop` (LOW-TO-CRITICAL SECURITY AUDITOR)
# =============================================================================

Source file: `skills/security-redteam-loop/SKILL.md`

---
name: security-redteam-loop
description: Deep Low-to-Critical application security auditor for vibe-coded apps. Performs multi-file data-flow analysis, STRIDE threat modeling, OWASP Top 10 auditing, BaaS/RLS verification, payment flow validation, and AI/LLM endpoint hardening.
---

# Security Red-Team Loop — Low-to-Critical Vulnerability Auditor

Perform a thorough, defensive architectural and source-code security audit tailored to the exact failure modes of AI-generated ("vibe-coded") applications.

## Audit Checklist Across 5 Trust Boundaries

### 1. Secrets, Environment & Supply Chain (`CRITICAL` / `HIGH`)

- Verify no private keys, database connection strings, or service-role keys appear in client-bundled env vars (`NEXT_PUBLIC_*`, `VITE_*`, `EXPO_PUBLIC_*`, `REACT_APP_*`).
- Check git history and root files for committed `.env`, `.pem`, `.key`, or hardcoded bearer tokens.
- Verify all package dependencies in `package.json` or `requirements.txt` are legitimate packages (catching AI-hallucinated "slopsquatting" package names).

### 2. Authentication, Session & Access Control (`CRITICAL`)

- Enumerate every API route (`app/api/**`, `pages/api/**`, FastAPI `@app.post/put/delete`, Express routers) and every Next.js Server Action (`"use server"`).
- Confirm each route verifies the caller's session on the server before executing logic.
- Trace every database read/write that accepts an `id`, `userId`, `orgId`, or `slug` from the request. Confirm the query filters by the authenticated session owner (`WHERE id = $1 AND user_id = $2` or enforced RLS) to prevent **Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR)**.
- Check that JWTs are verified with `jwt.verify()` (never just `jwt.decode()`) and session tokens are stored in `HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite` cookies rather than `localStorage`.

### 3. Database & Backend-as-a-Service (Supabase / Firebase / SQL / Prisma) (`CRITICAL` / `HIGH`)

- Inspect all `.sql` migrations: every table in the `public` schema must enable Row-Level Security (`ALTER TABLE ... ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;`) and define granular policies. Flag any `USING (true)` policy on write operations or sensitive tables.
- Inspect `firestore.rules` / `database.rules.json`: flag `allow read, write: if true`.
- Check for raw SQL interpolation (`$queryRawUnsafe`, template literals inside `.query()`, Python `f"SELECT ..."`).

### 4. Payments, Webhooks & Business Logic (`CRITICAL` / `HIGH`)

- Trace Stripe, Razorpay, LemonSqueezy, or PayPal checkout creation: confirm prices, plan IDs, and trial eligibility are resolved on the server from trusted constants or database records—never from client request bodies.
- Confirm webhook endpoints verify cryptographic signatures (`stripe.webhooks.constructEvent`) using the raw unparsed request body and enforce idempotency against replay of already-processed `event.id`s.
- Check for race conditions (TOCTOU) in credit balances, coupon redemptions, or quota counters (require atomic `UPDATE ... SET credits = credits - 1 WHERE credits >= 1`).

### 5. AI/LLM Endpoints, Network & Deployment Posture (`HIGH` / `MEDIUM` / `LOW`)

- For apps calling OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, or open-weight models: verify authentication, per-user rate limits, explicit `max_tokens` / `maxTokens` caps, and separation between untrusted user data and system instructions.
- Check URL-fetching endpoints for Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) against internal metadata services (`169.254.169.254`, `localhost`).
- Verify production configuration sets `Content-Security-Policy`, `Strict-Transport-Security`, `X-Frame-Options`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, and strict CORS origins.

---

# =============================================================================
# PART 5: SKILL - `ui-ux-bug-finder` (UI/UX, LAYOUT & ACCESSIBILITY AUDITOR)
# =============================================================================

Source file: `skills/ui-ux-bug-finder/SKILL.md`

---
name: ui-ux-bug-finder
description: Comprehensive UI/UX design, interaction flow, responsive layout, and WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility bug finder for vibe-coded apps. Detects dead buttons, missing loading/empty/error states, mobile overflow traps, z-index collisions, and live DOM layout defects.
---

# UI/UX Design & Browser QA Bug Finder

Audit frontend code and live rendered pages to catch the visual, interaction, state-management, and accessibility bugs frequently introduced during vibe coding.

## 5-Point UI/UX Inspection Protocol

### 1. Interactive Wiring & Dead Control Detection (`HIGH`)

- Scan all `<button>`, `<a>`, `<form>`, dropdowns, and action cards across every page/route.
- Flag any control with `href="#"`, missing `onClick` / `type="submit"`, or stubbed handlers (`() => {}` or `console.log`).

**Separate three distinct bugs - they have three different fixes:**

| Pattern | Rule | Why it is wrong | Fix |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `<a href="#">Terms</a>` | `UX-01` | Goes nowhere | Give it a real destination |
| `<a href="#" onClick={del}>` | `UX-11` | Announced as "link" so the user expects navigation; Space does not activate it; `#` jumps to top and pollutes history | `<button type="button" onClick={del}>` |
| `<div onClick={go}>` | `UX-12` | Not focusable, not keyboard operable, announced as plain text | `<button type="button">` |

The principle: **if it performs an action it is a button; if it navigates it is a link with a real `href`.** Choose the right element and the browser gives you focus, Tab order, Enter *and* Space, and the correct role for free. Retrofitting a `<div>` requires `role="button"` **and** `tabIndex={0}` **and** an `onKeyDown` handling both Enter and Space - three things to get right instead of zero, which is why the real button is the better answer.

Do not flag a `<div>` that already carries `role`, `tabIndex` and a key handler - that is a correct retrofit.
- Verify every modal, drawer, and dialog has a working close button, `Escape` key dismissal, and cleans up body scroll locks on unmount.

### 2. Async State Matrix Completeness (`HIGH` / `MEDIUM`)

Verify that every component performing an async fetch or mutation explicitly implements all 4 states:
- **Loading State**: Skeleton loader or spinner shown; submit/action buttons set `disabled={isLoading}` to prevent duplicate submissions.
- **Empty State**: When a list or query returns `0` items, render a helpful empty state with a clear call-to-action instead of a blank void.
- **Error State**: When a fetch or mutation fails, catch the error and display a user-friendly alert, toast, or inline field error with a retry option (never swallow errors in an empty `catch {}`).
- **Success Feedback**: Confirm mutations give clear visual confirmation (toast, redirect, or optimistic UI update).

### 3. Responsive Layout & Mobile Viewport Audit (`MEDIUM`)

- Check layout behavior at **Mobile (`375x812`)**, **Tablet (`768x1024`)**, and **Desktop (`1440x900`)**.
- Flag hardcoded pixel widths (`w-[600px]`, `min-w-[500px]`, `width: 800px`), un-wrapped wide tables (`overflow-x-auto` missing), or `100vw` containers that cause horizontal scrolling on mobile.
- Ensure touch targets (buttons, nav links, close icons) are at least `44x44px` on mobile screens and do not overlap with fixed bottom bars or floating action buttons.

### 4. Accessibility & Keyboard Ergonomics — WCAG 2.2 AA (`MEDIUM` / `LOW`)

- Verify every `<input>`, `<select>`, and `<textarea>` is linked to a visible `<label>` or `aria-label`.
- Verify every icon-only `<button>` has an `aria-label` and every `<img />` has an `alt` attribute.
- Check color contrast pairings (avoid low-contrast muted text like `text-gray-300` on `bg-white` or `text-gray-600` on `bg-gray-900`).
- Ensure keyboard `Tab` order is logical and focus indicators (`focus-visible:ring-2`) are never stripped without replacement.

### 5. Live Browser DOM Inspection (When Dev Server + Browser Tool Available)

If the app is running locally and `agent-browser` or Playwright is installed:
```bash
agent-browser open http://localhost:3000
agent-browser set viewport 375 812
agent-browser snapshot
agent-browser screenshot --annotate .aegis/mobile-audit.png
agent-browser set viewport 1440 900
agent-browser screenshot --annotate .aegis/desktop-audit.png
agent-browser close
```
Inspect the accessibility tree and screenshots to verify zero overlapping elements, zero console errors, and clean visual alignment.

---

# =============================================================================
# PART 7: SCANNER CLI REFERENCE - `scripts/aegis_scan.py`
# =============================================================================

Zero-dependency Python 3.8+ static and passive-live scanner. No pip install required.

## Usage

```text
python3 scripts/aegis_scan.py [target] [--url URL] [--json] [--output PATH] [--fail-on-high]
```

## Arguments

**Output**

| Argument | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `target` | `.` | Path to the repository to scan. Exits `2` if it does not exist. |
| `--json` | off | Print the full JSON report to stdout. |
| `--output <PATH>` | none | Write the JSON report to a file. Parent directories are created. |
| `--sarif <PATH>` | none | Write SARIF 2.1.0 so findings appear in GitHub's Security tab. |
| `--sbom <PATH>` | none | Write a CycloneDX 1.5 SBOM of detected dependencies. |
| `--quiet` | off | Print only the one-line summary. |

**Release gate**

| Argument | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `--fail-on-high` | Exit `1` if any `CRITICAL` or `HIGH` finding exists. |
| `--fail-on <level>` | Exit `1` at or above `critical`/`high`/`medium`/`low`. |

**Scope - how a team adopts this on an existing codebase**

| Argument | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `--diff [REF]` | Scan only files changed vs `REF` (default `origin/main`). Use for pull requests. |
| `--baseline <PATH>` | Suppress findings recorded in a baseline file. |
| `--write-baseline <PATH>` | Accept all current findings as pre-existing; future scans show only new issues. |

Also honoured: a `.aegis-ignore` file in the repo root, one entry per line, either a rule id
(`SEC-03`) or a path glob (`src/legacy/**`).

**Deep analysis**

| Argument | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `--artifact [PATH]` | Verify a build directory or an `.apk`/`.aab`/`.ipa`. Auto-detects `dist/`, `build/`, `out/`, `.next/`, `.output/`, `.svelte-kit/`. |
| `--git-history [N]` | Hunt credentials committed in the last `N` commits (default 300). |
| `--deps` | Check dependencies against the OSV vulnerability database. |
| `--url <URL>` | Passive, read-only live header and exposure checks. |
| `--all` | Enable artifacts + git history + dependencies. |
| `--offline` | Never make a network request. |

## Exit Codes

| Code | Meaning |
| :--- | :--- |
| `0` | Scan completed with no blocking findings, or no gate flag was set. |
| `1` | A gate flag was set and a finding met the threshold. |
| `2` | The target path does not exist. |

## Common Invocations

```bash
# Everything, machine-readable, for an agent or CI pipeline
python3 scripts/aegis_scan.py . --all --output .aegis/scan-report.json

# Verify what actually ships before deploying or uploading
python3 scripts/aegis_scan.py . --artifact dist/
python3 scripts/aegis_scan.py . --artifact app/build/outputs/apk/release/app-release.apk

# Pull-request review: only what changed, minus pre-existing noise
python3 scripts/aegis_scan.py . --diff origin/main --baseline .aegis/baseline.json --quiet

# First adoption on a large existing repo
python3 scripts/aegis_scan.py . --write-baseline .aegis/baseline.json

# GitHub code scanning + SBOM
python3 scripts/aegis_scan.py . --all --sarif .aegis/results.sarif --sbom .aegis/sbom.json

# CI merge gate
python3 scripts/aegis_scan.py . --fail-on-high
```

## What `--url` Actually Does

Strictly passive and read-only. It issues:

1. One `GET` to the supplied URL, reading response headers only. It checks for
   `Content-Security-Policy`, `X-Frame-Options`, `X-Content-Type-Options`,
   `Strict-Transport-Security` (HTTPS targets only), and a wildcard
   `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`.
2. One `GET` each to `/.env` and `/.git/config` to detect accidental public exposure,
   reading at most 512 bytes of the response.

It sends the User-Agent `VibeAegis-PreLaunch-Audit/1.0 (Passive-Read-Only)`, no credentials,
no payloads, and no `POST`/`PUT`/`DELETE`. It does not crawl or spider. If the URL is
unreachable the scanner records a `LIVE-00` LOW informational finding rather than failing.

**Only use `--url` against deployments you own or are authorized to test.**

## Release Readiness Score

The score starts at `100` and subtracts a weight per finding, floored at `0`:

| Severity | Penalty |
| :--- | :--- |
| `CRITICAL` | 25 |
| `HIGH` | 10 |
| `MEDIUM` | 4 |
| `LOW` | 1 |

| Condition | `release_verdict` |
| :--- | :--- |
| Any `CRITICAL` or `HIGH` present | `BLOCKED (Fix Critical/High findings before publishing)` |
| Score >= 90 and no blockers | `READY TO PUBLISH` |
| Score < 90 and no blockers | `NEEDS REVIEW (Address Medium/Low polish items)` |

## Rule Identifier Reference

- `SEC-01` .. `SEC-17` - security rules, `domain` is `SECURITY`.
- `SEC-17B` - live server exposure of `/.env` or `/.git/config`, `CRITICAL`.
- `LIVE-00` - the supplied `--url` could not be reached, `LOW`, informational only.
- `UX-01` .. `UX-10` - UI/UX rules, `domain` is `UI_UX`.
- `FLOW-01` .. `FLOW-05` - data-flow (taint) findings, `domain` is `DATAFLOW`, confidence `MEDIUM` by design.
- `DEP-00`/`DEP-01` - dependency vulnerabilities, `domain` is `SUPPLY_CHAIN`.
- `ART-01` .. `ART-15` - build artifact and mobile package findings, `domain` is `ARTIFACT`.
  `ART-01` is confirmed by construction (same credential present in both source and bundle) and must not be dismissed.
- `HIST-01` - credentials found in git history, `domain` is `HISTORY`.

## Reports Are Safe To Share

Every credential in every output format is redacted to its first 6 and last 4 characters plus a
length. `.aegis/scan-report.json` can be committed, attached to an issue, or handed to an agent
without leaking the value it is warning about.

---

# =============================================================================
# PART 8: JSON REPORT SCHEMA - `.aegis/scan-report.json`
# =============================================================================

Produced by `--output`. Validate with `schemas/scan-report.schema.json`
(JSON Schema Draft 2020-12). Top-level keys: `scanner`, `version`, `timestamp`,
`target_path`, `live_url`, `scanned_files`, `tech_stack`, `readiness_score`,
`release_verdict`, `summary_counts`, `findings`.

Each entry in `findings` has: `rule_id`, `domain` (`SECURITY` or `UI_UX`),
`severity` (`CRITICAL`/`HIGH`/`MEDIUM`/`LOW`), `title`, `file`, `line`, `snippet`,
`cwe_or_standard`, `remediation`, `confidence`.

Findings arrive pre-sorted: severity first (CRITICAL to LOW), then domain, file, line.

## Full Schema

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "$id": "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Tacuns/vibe-aegis/main/schemas/scan-report.schema.json",

  "description": "Deterministic output of `python3 scripts/aegis_scan.py <target> --json --output .aegis/scan-report.json`. CI pipelines and AI agents can validate scan output against this schema before acting on it.",

  "additionalProperties": false,

      ]
    },
    "summary_counts": {
      "description": "Finding tallies by severity and by domain.",
      "type": "object",
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "required": [
        "CRITICAL",
        "HIGH",
        "MEDIUM",
        "LOW",
        "SECURITY_TOTAL",
        "UI_UX_TOTAL",
        "SUPPLY_CHAIN_TOTAL",
        "ARTIFACT_TOTAL",
        "HISTORY_TOTAL",
        "DATAFLOW_TOTAL",
        "SUPPRESSED",
        "PAYMENTS_TOTAL",
        "RELIABILITY_TOTAL"
      ],
      "properties": {
        "CRITICAL": {
          "type": "integer",
          "minimum": 0
        },
        "HIGH": {
          "type": "integer",
          "minimum": 0
        },
        "MEDIUM": {
          "type": "integer",
          "minimum": 0

          "type": "string",
          "pattern": "^(SEC|UX|LIVE|DEP|ART|HIST|GIT|FLOW|PAY|REL)-[0-9]{2}[A-Z]?$"
        },

            "ARTIFACT",
            "HISTORY",
            "DATAFLOW"
          ]
        },
        "severity": {
          "description": "Impact rating used by the Release Readiness Score.",
          "enum": [
            "CRITICAL",
            "HIGH",
            "MEDIUM",
            "LOW"
          ]
        },
        "title": {
          "description": "Short human-readable description of the defect.",
          "type": "string",
          "minLength": 1
        },
        "file": {
          "description": "Repository-relative file path, or the probed URL for live posture findings.",
          "type": "string",
          "minLength": 1
        },
        "line": {
          "description": "1-indexed line number, or 0 for findings that are not tied to a source line (live URL checks).",
          "type": "integer",
          "minimum": 0
        },
        "snippet": {
          "description": "Trimmed evidence excerpt. Credentials are always redacted (first 6 and last 4 characters only) so reports are safe to commit and share.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "cwe_or_standard": {
          "description": "Cited authority: a CWE ID, an OWASP Top 10 category, or a WCAG 2.2 success criterion.",
          "type": "string",
          "minLength": 1
        },
        "remediation": {
          "description": "Concrete, actionable fix instruction.",
          "type": "string",
          "minLength": 1
        },
        "confidence": {
          "description": "Scanner confidence before the adversarial Skeptic stage reviews the claim.",
          "enum": [
            "HIGH",
            "MEDIUM",
            "LOW"
          ],
          "default": "HIGH"
        },
        "fingerprint": {
          "description": "Stable 16-hex-character id derived from rule, file and normalised evidence. Used for baseline suppression and SARIF partialFingerprints; survives line-number shifts.",
          "type": "string",
          "pattern": "^[0-9a-f]{16}$"
        },
        "kind": {
          "description": "'finding' is a real defect that counts toward the score. 'skipped_check' is a check that could not run - it never affects the score and forces an INCOMPLETE verdict.",

            "skipped_check"
          ],
          "default": "finding"

          "enum": [
            "VULNERABILITY",
            "SKIPPED",
            "SCAN_ERROR"
          ],
          "default": "VULNERABILITY"
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```
